What, then, is the meaning of the pillar of fire? At night, when it is dark, we need the fire. Yet its meaning is the same as that of the cloud. The cloud is fire, and the fire is cloud. When the sun shines, the Lord’s presence is like the appearance of a cloud; when darkness falls, it is like the appearance of fire. It is one and the same thing, only with different forms of appearance.

If that is so, what does the fire signify? It signifies the Word. The cloud is the Spirit, and the fire is the Word. When the sun is shining, you can see very clearly in the Spirit, and you can follow the cloud quite easily. But many times it is just like night, and you are in deep darkness. You may not even be able to trust your own spirit; your spirit may be greatly oppressed. In such a situation, you must rely on the Word. The Word is like a burning fire, shining and giving us light. Psalm 119:105 says, “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.” When the sky is very clear and everything is bright, the cloud is enough. But when darkness covers the sky and you cannot distinguish which is cloud and which is not, then you must follow the Fire.

ANDAMAN & NICOBAR ISLAND PRESS STUDY TOUR

Today, under the arrangement of the Information & Public Relations Department, 9 members of the Mizoram Journalists Association and 3 I&PR officials left Aizawl for a Press Study Tour to the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

During the Press Study Tour in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, the participants will study various government initiatives and will also meet government officials.

The Press Study Tour will be held from December 9, 2019 to December 15, 2019.

Selected MJA members from different districts of Mizoram are taking part, and they are being led by I&PR Director Pi Lallianpuii, MIS, and Joint Director (Admn) Pu C. Lalnunkima, MIS.

raw_text:
UNION MINISTER SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA HOLDS MEETING IN MAMIT 882/2022-2023 Mamit, 13th June, 2022: Shri Parshottam Rupala, Hon’ble Union Cabinet Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, today held an interaction at the DC Conference Hall, Mamit, with government officials within Mamit town and beneficiaries of various Central Schemes.

At today’s meeting, chaired by Pu Lalnunhlua, Deputy Commissioner, Pu Lalsanglura, Nodal Officer for the Aspirational District Programme, gave a detailed presentation using PowerPoint on the various initiatives being undertaken under the Aspirational District Programme. This was followed by discussion on the progress made and the various future plans and targets.

Shri Parshottam Rupala, Union Minister, explained the reason for his visit to Mamit District and for holding the meeting, saying that he had come to review whether the people of the district were benefiting from the various Central Schemes and whether these were being implemented properly, and to understand and help resolve any difficulties being faced. He also encouraged the district’s concerned officers to study the various government programmes carefully and to work so that the beneficiaries could fully avail themselves of them.

He said that since Mamit District is an Aspirational District, the Centre has made provisions for treatment of serious illnesses with bills up to Rs. 5 lakh, and that out of 5,000 selected persons in Mamit District, 3,000 had already been selected to receive the benefit, while efforts were underway so that the remaining 2,000 could also receive it. He also said that PM-Kisan can be applied for by those who have an Aadhaar Card, land, and a bank account, and urged the concerned departments to ensure that as many farmers as possible in Mamit District receive benefits under the scheme.

The Union Minister said that he would try, as far as possible, to address the problems and needs raised by the government officials and beneficiaries during today’s interaction.

On this occasion, there was also an interaction and question-and-answer session with beneficiaries and concerned officials under various Central Schemes including AYUSHMAN BHARAT - Health & Wellness, Ayushman Bharat - Jan Arogya Yojana, e-Transaction, Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), PM Street Vendor’s Atma Nirbhar Nidhi (PM-SVANidhi

raw_text:
DRAFT ELECTORAL ROLL 2020 PUBLISHED IN LAWNGTLAI

The draft electoral roll for the three Assembly constituencies in Lawngtlai District for 2020 was published yesterday (16.12.2019) by the Lawngtlai District Election Officer, who is also the Deputy Commissioner of Lawngtlai, Pi Shashanka Ala, IAS, in her office chamber. The draft roll was also handed over to representatives of political parties.

According to the published draft electoral roll, in 36-Tuichawng (ST) A/C there are 15,852 male voters and 15,520 female voters, making a total of 31,372; in 37-Lawngtlai West (ST) A/C there are 13,524 male voters and 13,402 female voters, making a total of 26,926; in 38-Lawngtlai East (ST) A/C there are 11,626 male voters and 12,374 female voters, making a total of 24,000. Altogether, in the three Assembly constituencies there are 41,002 male voters and 41,296 female voters, making a total of 82,298 voters.

For this summary revision, time has been given until January 15 of the new year for those who wish to make claims or objections. The final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on February 7, 2020.

raw_text:
Today, as part of the observance of Children’s Week in Mamit, the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit District, organized a Fun Day programme at GSA Playground, Mamit, using the theme “Happy Childhood” as the opening event of Children’s Week.

Pu Shashank Jaiswal, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Mamit, inaugurated the programme and expressed his appreciation to the District Child Protection Unit, Mamit. He said it was commendable and encouraging that they had arranged such an event so that the children of Mamit could spend their time happily. He also said that the safety and happiness of the children of our land rests in everyone’s hands, and at the same time emphasized the importance of cooperation among adults and the community and the need for all to work together. He further stated that if children within Mamit District face any difficulties, the Mamit Police are always there to help them at any time. He encouraged those gathered to make use of such occasions so that children may enjoy memorable, pleasant and happy moments, and to use them as opportunities to further strengthen child protection.

The programme was led by Pi Vanlalruati, PO(IC), DCPU, and Dr. R. Lalrinhlua, DCPO, also spoke about why the Fun Day had been organized for the children of Mamit town and about the importance of giving children leisure time and rest. He said that since children are the future leaders of our country, it is our responsibility to care for them diligently.

At this Fun Day, the DCPU engaged the children with various entertainment activities such as Bouncy, Trampoline, See Saw, Mega Block, Ball Pool, and different games including Spin the Wheel, Ball Kick, Dart Game, Cup Game, Ball Score, Photo Booth, Talent Hunt, and Bow and Arrow. Child Care Institutions also set up different stalls and made these recreational activities available for children to enjoy free of charge.

The children greatly valued the event, and a large number of children from Mamit town attended.

Principal Secretary, Higher & Technical Education Department leh Chairman State Selection Board Committee ni bawk chuan thuchhuah siamin State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022 atana online a dilna thehluh hun tawp ni (last date of submission) chu Zirtawpni, June ni 3, 2022 zan 11:50 thlenga pawhsei a ni tiin he exam bei tum zirlaite a hriattir a. reference: Government of Mizoram postpone Smartee Exam 47/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 11th May 2022; As shown below, the Government of Mizoram postponed the date of examination for State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022. The last date & time of submission of online application form for State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022 notified vide this Office Order No.A.45011/2/2021-JDT(HTE) dated Aizawl, the 11th April, 2022 is hereby extended up to the 3rd June, 2022 (Friday) 11:59 pm. Further, the date of examination of SMATEE 2022 is also hereby postponed on the 17th June,2022 (Friday) between 11:00 am - 2:00 pm.
hypothesis: Government postpones SMATEE Exam 471/2022-2023 Aizawl, 11th May 2022: As stated below, the Government of Mizoram has postponed the scheduled date for holding the State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022. The Principal Secretary, Higher & Technical Education Department, who is also the Chairman of the State Selection Board Committee, stated in a press release that the last date for submitting online applications for the State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022 has been extended till 11:50 p.m. on Friday, 3rd June 2022, and informed students intending to appear for the exam accordingly. He also informed that the SMATEE 2022 exam has been rescheduled to Friday, 17th June 2022.

The Principal Secretary, Higher & Technical Education Department, who is also the Chairman of the State Selection Board Committee, stated in a press release that the last date for submitting online applications for the State Medical and Technical Entrance Examination (SMATEE) 2022 has been extended till 11:50 p.m. on Friday, 3rd June 2022, and informed students intending to appear for the exam accordingly. He also informed that the SMATEE 2022 exam has been rescheduled to Friday, 17th June 2022.

hypothesis: Life was created to be capable of being corrupted and defiled. For example, suppose we instruct our children at home not to play with the blackboard chalk. After I leave the house, out of sheer curiosity they play with the chalk; then when I return, I discover that they have done wrong. Their wrongdoing is only a violation of household rules, and nothing has entered into them. However, suppose on another occasion I leave at home a bottle containing very dangerous medicine and tell the children, “Do not ever drink this.” After I leave the house, they discover that the bottle is very tempting to open—and in the end they drink the very dangerous poisonous medicine. Here, they have not merely broken the family rule and disobeyed my command; worse than that, something dangerous has entered into them. In exactly this way, when Adam ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, this is what happened. He not only disobeyed what God had forbidden, but Satan’s life also entered into him. At that very point, man’s inward being became thoroughly corrupted; besides the good, upright, and proper human life he originally had, he also came to possess the corrupted and sinful life of Satan.

source: COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES MINISTER-IN LUNGLEIAH AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING HAWNG No.4122/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 26 th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana chuan vawiin khan Electric Veng, Lungleiah NABARD sum cheng nuai 1082.93 senga ruahman Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building a hawng. Hawnna inkhawm Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi kaihhruaiah Dr R Lalthangliana chuan Lunglei khawpui chhunga hmasawnna ruhrel liantham, khawtlang tana chhenfakawm tak leh eizawnna kawnga tangkai taka hman theih tur Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building zawhfel a ni chu lawmawm tiin a buaipuitu Commerce & Industries thawktute, building sa tu te leh Electric Veng Lunglei khawtlang te chungah lawmthu a sawi a. C&I Department hnuaiah hmalakna hrang hrang kalpui mek zel anih thu sawiin Lunglei Supermarket sakna tur cheng nuai 1400 NEC atanga sanction hmuh anih thu sawiin Bangladesh ram nena kan insumdawn tawnna atana ruahman Integrated Check Post (ICP), Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung ti hlawhtling turin Department chuan theihtawp a chhuah mek zel thu a sawi a ni. A Department chan dangte hnuaia hmalaknte pawh sawilangin Minister chuan MZU Southern Campus atan DPR cheng vaibelchhe 400 sawrkar laipuiah thehluh tawh niin chak taka bawhzui mek a ni a, MZU Southern Campus tana hman lailawk tur Engineering College building chei that hna pawh thawh mek a ni, a ti a. Civil Hospital Lungleia Trauma Centre sak pawh zawh fel thuai beisei anih thu sawiin Multipurpose Laboratory Building, NEC sum cheng nuai 300 a ruahman mek pawh nakum kum tir lama zawhfel beisei anih thu a sawi. Lunglei Municipal Council (LMC) chungchang pawh sawiin Minister chuan Municipal body chak tak enkawlna hnuaiah Lunglei khawpui chuan kawng hrang hrangin hmasawnna a nei dawn a ni, a ti. He huna khualzahawm Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng chuan Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building hawn theiha peih fel a ni ta chu Pathian malsawmna ropui tak a ni tiin he hmasawnna ruhrel neih theihna tura sulsutute thawhrimna leh thahnemngaihna rah a ni, a ti a. He building ti hlawhtling tura bultan tu Pu Joseph Lalhimpuia chungah leh a hmun phal taka petu Electric Veng YMA te chungah lawmthu a sawi a ni. He building sak enkawltu AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl atangin Technical Report ngaihtlak a ni a. Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure hi NABARD, RIDF XXIII hnuaia project niin total project cost hi Rs. 1082.93 lakhs ani a. Hna hi 05/10/2018 ah thawh tan a ni. A building plinth area hi 574.875 Square metres niin building hi floor nga (5) a sak a ni a. First floor hi Agriculture leh marketing lama training leh awareness centre atan ruahman niin mihring 300 vel leng tura hisap a ni. Ground floor ah hian guest room, conference/meeting room te awmin Basement I ah hian mi 78 lenna market area bakah market office ruamhan niin Basement II ah mi 85 lenna market area niin Basement III hi motor 25 lenna parking area-a ruahman a ni. reference: AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING INAUGURATED AT LUNGLEI No.523/2021-2022 Aizawl, the 28th February 2022 : Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana on Saturday (26th February, 2022) inaugurated Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei. The Rs. 1082.93 lakhs project is implemented under the NABARD, RIDF XXIII. Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng was the guest of honour at the inauguration. At the inaugural function chaired by Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary, Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi, Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr R Lalthangliana commended C&I Department staff, Electric veng YMA, VCs for their contribution towards successful completion of the project. As per Technical Report presented by AIE Constructions, Tuikhuahtlang, Aizawl, the 5 floors Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building has a plinth area of 574.875 Square metres. The first floor is intended to be used as a training and awareness centre for agriculture marketing with an estimated capacity of 300 people, with guest rooms, conference/meeting rooms at the Ground floor. Basement I and Basement II contain the market areas and market offices, with a parking area at the basement.

raw_text:
COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES MINISTER OPENS AGRI-MARKETING & TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDING IN LUNGLEI

No.4122/2021-2022  
Aizawl, the 26th February 2022:

Today, Commerce & Industries (C&I) Minister Dr. R. Lalthangliana inaugurated the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building at Electric Veng, Lunglei, constructed at a cost of Rs. 1082.93 lakhs under NABARD funding.

At the inauguration function, chaired by Commerce & Industries Department Commissioner & Secretary Pi Esther Lal Ruatkimi, Dr. R. Lalthangliana expressed happiness over the completion of the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building, which he described as a major development asset within Lunglei town, something commendable for the local community, and one that can be usefully utilized for livelihood purposes. He thanked the Commerce & Industries staff who worked on it, those who constructed the building, and the residents of Electric Veng, Lunglei.

He said that various initiatives are continuously being undertaken under the C&I Department. He mentioned that Rs. 1400 lakhs has been sanctioned by NEC for the construction of the Lunglei Supermarket, and that the Department is making every effort to successfully implement the proposed Integrated Check Post (ICP) at Kawrpuichhuah, Tlabung, intended for trade with Bangladesh.

Referring also to initiatives under other departments, the Minister said that a DPR worth Rs. 400 crore for MZU Southern Campus has already been submitted to the central government and is being actively pursued. Renovation work on the Engineering College building, to be used temporarily for MZU Southern Campus, is also underway, he said.

He further stated that the Trauma Centre at Civil Hospital, Lunglei is expected to be completed soon, and that the Multipurpose Laboratory Building, being planned under NEC funding of Rs. 300 lakhs, is also expected to be completed in the early part of next year.

Speaking about the Lunglei Municipal Council (LMC), the Minister said that under the strong administration of the municipal body, Lunglei town will see progress in various ways.

On this occasion, the chief guest, Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, said that the completion and opening of the Agri-Marketing & Training Infrastructure Building was a great blessing from God, and that this development project was the fruit of the hard work and dedication

raw_text:
RAJYA SABHA MP PU K. VANLALVENA SUBMITS THE ISSUE OF THE SUFFERING OF THE PEOPLE OF MYANMAR TO THE VICE PRESIDENT OF INDIA

No. 7795/2020-2021  
Aizawl, 15th March, 2021:

Rajya Sabha MP Pu K. Vanlalvena, who is currently in Delhi for the Parliament Budget Session, today called on the Vice President of India and also Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu, at his residence and discussed with him the severe suffering being faced by those striving to restore democracy in Myanmar, along with other important needs of Mizoram. Pu Vena was accompanied by MNF Adviser Pu Rosangzuala.

He informed the Vice President that because of the crisis in Myanmar, many people had already been killed and injured at the hands of the military, many had been imprisoned, that the exact number of those killed and injured due to the unrest could not yet be known, and that the numbers appeared likely to continue increasing. He also told him that some members of the Myanmar military and police, unwilling to act against the people of Myanmar, had surrendered their arms and, along with some other civilians, had fled to Mizoram seeking refuge.

They also conveyed that it was necessary to consider assistance for these refugees fleeing from Myanmar, and appealed to the Vice President of India to take appropriate steps to bring an end to the suffering of the people of Myanmar. They further stated that they felt it was necessary to review the Central Government’s policy toward Myanmar.

Pu Vena and Pu Rosangzuala also requested the Vice President to help ensure that a Mizo person be appointed to the Union Public Service Commission, since not even one person from Mizoram has ever served as a member of the UPSC since India became independent. They also informed the Vice President that even after 35 years of attaining full statehood, Mizoram still remains under the AGMUT cadre in the All India Civil Services, which they said was no longer appropriate, and that the time had come to create a separate Mizoram cadre.

They also requested Vice President Pu M. Venkaiah Naidu to consider making it possible for applicants for jobs under the Staff Selection Commission to take their examinations in Aizawl, so that they would no longer have to go all the way to Guwahati for the exams.

reference: VDVK LEVEL ADVOCACY PROGRAMME ON PMVDY HELD AT KAWRTHAH No.342/2021-2022 Aizawl 8th October, 2021 : Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK) Level Advocacy Programme under Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (PMVDY) was held at SSA Block Resource Centre at Kawrthah Mamit District under the leadership of Pu Lalthangfala, District Cooperative Officer Mamit District. Under Kawrthah VDVK Centre targetted beneficiaries of 300 tribal women from Kawrthah cluster will be trained in tailoring. Awareness programme regarding VDVK under PMVDY was held for the trainees under the initiative of Mamit District Cooperative Office. Attachment Loading attachment...
hypothesis: PMVDY under VDVK Level Advocacy Programme held at Kawrthah. No.2537/2021-2022 Aizawl, 8th October, 2021: Today at Kawrthah village, under the Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (PMVDY), a VDVK Level Advocacy Programme and Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programme training was held. Pu Lalthangfala, District Cooperative Officer, Mamit, attended as chief guest and inaugurated the programme. The chief guest said that a weaving training centre for Mizo women would be opened at the Kawrthah village VDVK Centre and that weaving looms would be distributed under the Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (PMVDY). He urged the weaving trainees to be diligent and to take the training seriously as a means of livelihood. Today, this awareness programme was conducted for 300 women interested in weaving, in batches of 40 each, while observing Covid Appropriate Behaviour.

raw_text:
LUNGLEI DISTRICT - COVID-19 NO TOLERANCE FORTNIGHT No.6374/2020-2021

As the Covid-19 pandemic is spreading rapidly and there is a possibility of continued transmission, and in order that the public may be able to live in compliance with the restrictions imposed because of Covid-19, the Mizoram Government has planned the Covid-19 “No Tolerance Fortnight” from 26 October to 9 November 2020, and this is being strictly implemented in Lunglei District. At the same time, the Jan Andolan Campaign to educate people on safety measures relating to Covid-19 is also continuing.

Yesterday, under the leadership of Lunglei DC & DLTF Chairman Pu V. Lalsangliana, a meeting was held in his office chamber where the detailed manner of implementing the Covid-19 No Tolerance Fortnight in Lunglei District was discussed. During the No Tolerance Fortnight, 30 employees each from every government department have been assigned for Covid-19 Executive Duty, divided into 24 teams, and their duties have been arranged. Each team will have a Team Leader, and they will widely inform the public about guidelines for protection against Covid-19, and those who do not follow the guidelines will be fined without leniency.

These Covid-19 Executive Duty personnel will strictly enforce the provisions laid down for the public under The Mizoram (Containment and Prevention of Spread of Covid-19) Act, 2020 and the government orders issued thereunder, and against those found violating the law, penalty slips will be issued and proper challans prepared, and they will be made to pay the prescribed amount of fine. Lunglei District has also been divided into eight zones, and an Executive Magistrate/Incident Commander has been appointed for each zone.

hypothesis: In the whole world there has been at least one chosen of God who could say this: “The ruler of the world is coming, and he has nothing in me” (John 14:30). In other words, in the Lord Jesus there was not even the slightest trace of the prince of this world. What we must carefully note is that when the Lord Jesus came into this world, He did not come to be God, but to be man. God needed a man. If God Himself were to defeat Satan, it would be very easy; Satan would fall at once without delay. But God did not intend to do it Himself. To defeat Satan, He wanted a man; He intended that one creature should overcome another creature. When the Lord Jesus became man, He endured temptation just as a man does, and He passed through every kind of human experience. This man overcame; this man is the victor. He ascended on high and sat down at the right hand of God. Jesus was crowned with “glory and honor” (Heb. 2:9), and so He was exalted.
raw_text: In the whole world there has been at least one chosen of God who could say this: “The ruler of the world is coming, and he has nothing in me” (John 14:30). What we must carefully note is that when the Lord Jesus came into this world, He did not come to be God, but to be man. God needed a man. If God Himself were to defeat Satan, it would be very easy; Satan would fall at once without delay. But God did not intend to do it Himself. To defeat Satan, He wanted a man; He intended that one creature should overcome another creature. When the Lord Jesus became man, He endured temptation just as a man does, and He passed through every kind of human experience. This man overcame; this man is the victor. He ascended on high and sat down at the right hand of God. Jesus was crowned with “glory and honor” (Heb. 2:9), and so He was exalted.

reference: a) Post Devolution Revenue Deficit Grants: Revenue Deficit Grants are released as monthly installments to 17 States as per the recommendations of the Fifteenth Finance Commission to meet the gap in Revenue Accounts of the States post devolution.States which still show revenue deficit post devolution are recommended Revenue Deficit Grants. The Centre has put an estimated amount of ₹ 1,615.00 crore for 2022-23 as recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission which is 9.78% lower than the current year’s BE.The recommended Revenue Deficit Grants diminish towards the end of the Finance Commission award period with only ₹ 586.00 crore recommended for 2025-26.
hypothesis: a) Post Devolution Revenue Deficit Grant: The Finance Commission has provided for a Revenue Deficit Grant for seventeen States which it considered would still face a shortfall in meeting their expenditure even after receiving Tax Devolution, and accordingly the Central Government has budgeted Rs. 1,615.00 crore for Mizoram during 2022–23. reference: MIZORAM CHIEF SECRETARY LEADS GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES IN TAKING INTEGRITY PLEDGE 275/2023-2024 Vigilance Awareness Week, 2023 is to be observed in the whole of India from today, i.e. 30th October till 5th November, 2023. This year the theme is - 'Say no to corruption, commit to the Nation'. Starting off the Vigilance Week in Mizoram too, Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma led the officials and staff of the Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO this morning in taking the 'Integrity Pledge' in the Secretariat Courtyard. Likewise, all Heads of Offices under the State Government also led the employees in their respective offices in taking the Integrity Pledge, in which each government servant avowed to follow probity and rule of law in all walks of life, to neither take nor offer bribe, to perform all tasks in an honest and transparent manner, to act in public interest, to lead by example exhibiting integrity in personal behavior and to report any incident of corruption to the appropriate agency. raw_text:
MIZORAM CHIEF SECRETARY LEADS INTEGRITY PLEDGE OATH 2547/2023-2024

Vigilance Awareness Week, 2023 will be observed throughout India from 30th October to 5th November, 2023. This year’s Vigilance Week theme is “Say no to corruption, commit to the Nation.”

Along with other parts of the country, “Vigilance Week 2023” was inaugurated in Mizoram this morning, and under the leadership of Chief Secretary Dr. Renu Sharma, all government employees, officials and staff at the Mizoram Secretariat, MINECO, took the “Integrity Pledge” together in a gathering.

Heads of Office in every government office also took the “Integrity Pledge” together with the officers and staff working under them in their respective offices.

Through this Integrity Pledge, every government employee pledged to firmly fight corruption, to work honestly and transparently in accordance with government laws and instructions, to remember that their work is public service and to conduct themselves and perform their duties in a courteous manner worthy of emulation by others, and not to remain silent if they see or know of any corrupt practice, but to report it to the government.

Aspirational District atangin Mizoram District 11- te zingah pakhatna ni thei tura tan la tura chahin in tum tlat chuan theihloh a awm lo a ni tiin kum zabi 21-a hmasawnna chu hmang tangkaiin dik taka kan hmachhawn chuan District hnufual ber thin kha a ropui ber kan ni thei a ni a ti. HEALTH MINISTER HANDS OVER MOBILE MEDICAL VAN AND OTHER EQUIPMENT FOR USE IN MAMIT DISTRICT

VAILIAM No.7589/2020-2021

Today, Dr. R. Lalthangliana, Minister for Health & Family Welfare, Higher & Technical Education, Commerce & Industries, handed over a Mobile Medical Van, essential drugs, diagnostic kits, laptops and speakers for use at Mamit District Hospital, PHCs/CHCs and Sub-Centres.

Chief guest Dr. R. Lalthangliana said he was pleased that the people living in Mamit District had been provided with very useful equipment to help them advance in the field of health. He said that among the 11 districts, having a Medical Doctor as Deputy Commissioner who understands the importance of health is a great blessing. He urged them to strive to become the top district among Mizoram’s 11 districts after emerging from the Aspirational District category, saying that if they are determined, nothing is impossible. He added that if we make proper and effective use of the progress of the 21st century, even a district that is often considered backward can become the best.

Dr. Thangtea said it is a joy to be Mizo believers in God, and that the unity and cooperation inherited from our forefathers continue to bear good fruit. Though it is very painful that there have been deaths due to Covid-19, the success seen in our fight against the disease, and the fact that among the eight northeastern states of India Mizoram has the lowest number of deaths from Covid-19, is due to God and our collective effort.

The Minister encouraged those gathered not merely to look upward at the progress already achieved, but to take fresh initiative within their own capacity so that development may be steady and complete. He also said that steps are being taken to improve roads, and that road-cutting work has already begun from the eastern side toward the western side.

Er. H. Lalzirliana, local MLA, also expressed gratitude that very useful equipment had been purchased under CSR to help Mamit District advance in health and to enable it to come out of its Aspirational District status. He said the Deputy Commissioner’s initiative in this regard is commendable. HEALTH MINISTER ATTENDS IMA MIZORAM BRANCH CONFERENCE

Today, the Indian Medical Association (IMA) Mizoram State Branch held its 43rd Annual Conference at Aijal Club, with Health Minister Dr. R. Lalthangliana as the chief guest.

This year, the theme of the IMA Annual Conference was “Ending the HIV & AIDS Epidemic: Community by Community.”

Dr. R. Lalthangliana said that the government gives high priority to the health sector, and that health has also been given major importance in the SEDP, the Mizoram government’s flagship initiative. He said the government is open to progress in the health sector and is making strong efforts to build a solid foundation for advancement. The Minister said that the government is fully committed to every possible area of development, including the proposed Cancer Super Speciality Hospital at Zemabawk, improvement of ZMC, advancement of RIPANS, and progress in various hospitals and health-related sectors across Mizoram.

Dr. R. Lalthangliana said that doctors and nurses are public servants who perform important and honorable work, and he encouraged them to continue dedicating their knowledge and abilities for the welfare of the people. He also urged them to renew their commitment in this service, recognizing that beyond medical science and expertise, even kind words alone can bring healing to patients.

The conference opening programme was led by IMA President Dr. Rosangliana, and Honorary Secretary Dr. Chawnglungmuana presented a report on the association’s various activities.

The IMA Mizoram State Branch has 33 members, and also has 15 new intern members. Among its existing members, 15 have newly completed specialist degrees (MD/MS).

During this year, they received the IMA Special Award for Organizing (IMA North East Leaders Meet Conclave) and the President Appreciation Award (for IMA Membership Drive Trophy) from the IMA Headquarters.

The association regularly organizes special clinics in rural areas, where they examine patients free of charge with equipment and various medical tools. To promote advancement in medical knowledge, they also regularly organize various seminars for their members, and at this conference as well, they held detailed discussions on HIV and AIDS.

source: MYC CHAIRMAN IN SERKAWN LUNGLEIAH MYC INCUBATION CENTRE TUR LUNGPHUM A PHUM No.4413/2021-2022 Aizawl, 26 th March 2022 : Vawiin khan Lunglei North bialtu MLA, MYC Chairman Dr Vanlaltanpuia chuan Serkawn, Lungleiah Mizoram Youth Commission Incubation Centre tur lungphum a phum. MYC Incubation Centre hmun tur hi Lena Stadium bulah awmin a ram hi Serkawn VC te pek a ni. He hunah hian Lunglei High Powered Committee Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, Pu H. Lalnunzuala, Under Secretary MYC, Pu Lalrotluanga, President YMA Sub Hqrs Lunglei leh Serkawn khawtlang hruaitute leh tlawmngai pawl hrang hrang aiawhte an tel a ni. Mizoram Youth Commission Chairman Dr Vanlaltanpuia chuan MYC Incubation Centre-ah hian thalaite hmasawnna tura hmalakna hrang hrang â€“ competitive coaching, Information Technology, skill development leh entrepreneurship-te a len vek tur thu sawiin residential tura ruahman a nih thu a sawi a. Thalaite hmakhua ngaia an ram phal taka pe tu Serkawn khawtlang te chungah lawmthu sawiin an ram pek chu kan human resource tih hmasawnna kawngah leh kan ram economy than len zelna kawngah tangkai taka hman anih tur thu a sawi. A sawi zel naah MYC Chairman chuan Mizo thalaite hmasawnna turin MYC chuan theihtawp a chhuah zel dawn a ni tiin Lunglei, Siaha leh Kolasib District -ah te MYC Coaching Centre hawn tawh niin Champhai ah pawh hawn leh thuai tum a ni a. MYC Chairman lays foundation stone for MYC Incubation Centre at Serkawn, Lunglei

No. 4413/2021-2022  
Aizawl, 26th March 2022:

Today, Lunglei North MLA and MYC Chairman Dr. Vanlaltanpuia laid the foundation stone for the Mizoram Youth Commission Incubation Centre at Serkawn, Lunglei.

The site for the MYC Incubation Centre is located near Lena Stadium, and the land was donated by the Serkawn Village Council.

He further said that MYC would continue to do its utmost for the progress of Mizo youth. raw_text:
GOVT. ITI, AIZAWL HELD ITS CONVOCATION CEREMONY 1974/2022-2023  
Aizawl, 17th September, 2022:

Today, for the first time in Mizoram, Govt. ITI, Aizawl held a Convocation Programme for 143 ITI graduates.

Govt. ITI, Aizawl currently has 384 students in the ongoing 2022–23 session, and in the latest declared results it recorded an overall pass percentage of 97.14%. This is the best result since the establishment of Govt. ITI in Mizoram, and among various states across India, Govt. ITI, Aizawl also secured the sixth position.

At the convocation, certificates were presented to the 143 students.

At the Convocation Programme, Pu K. Lalhmingliana, Director of the LESDE Department, delivered the welcome address and expressed appreciation for the success of the outgoing students, which would help advance the world of skills in Mizoram.

The chief guest, Pu Lalramsanga Sailo, Secretary of the LESDE Department, said that he was greatly pleased that ITI education in Mizoram continues to progress and that Mizo youth are showing strong interest in skill-based learning. He said it is a matter of pride that Govt. ITI, Aizawl is counted among the high-performing Government ITIs in India. He also said that for the state to continue progressing, and for the youth to move forward toward becoming self-reliant through their skills, it is important to keep strengthening ITIs.

Most of the technician-level workers in Mizoram are graduates of Govt. ITI, Aizawl, and among the ITI graduates, 14 students from the Motor Mechanic Vehicle (MMV) trade received offers of appointment from major companies even before the results were declared.

Convocation had not previously been held nationwide, but from this year it has begun under the initiative of the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE). The convocation was held simultaneously in different parts of India, with the main function held in Delhi in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and it has been planned to be observed every year on Vishwakarma Day.

On this occasion, the chief guest presented awards to the Top 3 best-performing ITI outgoing students:
First - Lalpekthara, Electronics Mechanic
Second - F. Lalrammawia, Baker & Confectionery;

FINAL ELECTORAL ROLLS FOR USE IN THE TOKALO MDC CONSTITUENCY BY-ELECTION ANNOUNCED

Yesterday (15.10.2019) at 1:00 PM, the District Election Officer, who is also the Deputy Commissioner, Pu Bhupesh Chaudhary, IAS, announced in his office chamber the Final Electoral Rolls to be used for the MDC By-Election in Tokalo Constituency, and immediately handed over both hard and soft copies of the Final Electoral Rolls to representatives of various political parties.

This By-Election is to be held due to the demise of Tokalo constituency MDC Pu K.L. Bana. Using 1st January 2019 as the qualifying date, and as directed by the State Election Commission, the Summary Revision of the Electoral Rolls was carried out smoothly, and today had been fixed for the publication of the Final Electoral Rolls.

Present at the publication of the Final Electoral Rolls were Pu K. Vanlalthiana, Addl. DC; Pu Amol Srivastava, IAS, Assistant Commissioner; Pu H. Zonunmawia, Election Officer; Pu N. Vabeiratlua, DIPRO; representatives of Tlawmngai Pawl MTP(H) and MCHP(H); and representatives of various political parties.

According to the published Draft Electoral Rolls, in Tokalo constituency there are 450 women voters and 505 men voters, making a total of 955 voters.

SPORTS MINISTER FELICITATES THE NES U-19 TEAM

Headquarters 23 Sector Assam Rifles organized a felicitation programme today at Loch Hall, 46 Assam Rifles headquarters, to honor the Mizoram team that recently won the NES Under-19 Women’s Football Championship. Sports Minister Pu Robert Romawia Royte attended the function. Leaders of the Mizoram Football Association (MFA) were also present.

Speaking on the occasion, Sports Minister Pu Robert Romawia Royte congratulated the Mizoram U-19 women’s team on becoming champions of the NES U-19 Championship. He said that this victory does not belong only to the government, or to Assam Rifles as organizers and supporters, or to the MFA, but to all the people of Mizoram, and that the team is the pride of the people of Mizoram.

He further said that Mizoram’s women’s team defeating the Nagaland women’s team, which recently included players representing India at the international level, clearly showed the quality of our women footballers.

He said that the government would continue to support, encourage, and strengthen the initiatives taken by the MFA for the development of football as much as possible. He also invited MFA leaders to continue and strengthen the good cooperation between the government and the MFA.

Pu Robert Romawia Royte said that football is a very effective tool for national integration and strengthening unity. Because of football, relations between the northeastern states and other parts of India have improved, a better spirit of brotherhood has been created, and national unity has been strengthened. He said football’s potential is great and should not be underestimated.

He said that the government wants to promote not only football but also other sports disciplines more vigorously than before, and for that reason work is underway on a Mizoram Sports Policy, something the state has never had before. He expressed happiness at the progress of taekwondo, basketball, volleyball, and other sports disciplines, and said the government is giving serious thought to strengthening sports associations. He added that, as Sports Minister, he would do his utmost so that better planning and arrangements can be made.

He also stated that steps are being taken to install proper floodlighting at Rajiv Gandhi Sports Stadium so that international-level matches can be hosted there; that land is being searched for the construction of around four or five more football fields in Aizawl city; that sanction has already been granted for laying grass at Zembawk field; and that plans are also being made to lay grass at Khawzawl field

source: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati in Sainik School Chhingchhip a tlawh 2122/2022-2023 Chhingchhip, the 30th September 2022: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan vawiin khan Sainik School Chhingchhip a tlawh a. He hunah hian School building leh hmunhma te a endik a, Sikul naupangte hmaah fuihna thu a sawi bawk a ni. Governor hian Sainik School a thlenin amah zahna chibai 8 Bn Assam Rifles ten School kawtah an lo buk a. Wcdr Shahul Hameed, Principal leh Maj S.Kalyan, Administrative Officer ten zirtirtute leh School staff te an hmelhriattir chhunzawm a. Hemi zawh hian Principal Office ah Sainik School dinhmunte inhrilhhriatna hun neih leh a ni a. Assembly Hall-ah Official programme leh Cultural Programme neih chhunzawm nghal a ni. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan Principal leh a thawhpui ten Sainik School tha tak ni tur leh hmun danga Sainik School te dinhmun pha tura theihtawp an chhuah chu fakawm a tih thu a sawi hmasa a. Mizoram sawrkarin hetiang ang School tha bik Mizorama zirlaite tan a buatsaih thei chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi bawk a ni. raw_text:
Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visits Sainik School Chhingchhip

2122/2022-2023  
Chhingchhip, 30th September 2022:

Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visited Sainik School Chhingchhip today. During the visit, he inspected the school buildings and campus and also delivered words of encouragement to the students.

On the Governor’s arrival at Sainik School, a guard of honour was presented to him at the school gate by 8 Bn Assam Rifles. Wcdr Shahul Hameed, Principal, and Maj S. Kalyan, Administrative Officer, then introduced the teachers and school staff to him. After this, an interaction session on the status of the school was held in the Principal’s Office. This was immediately followed by the official programme and a cultural programme in the Assembly Hall.

Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati first said that the efforts being made by the Principal and his colleagues to make Sainik School an excellent institution and to bring it to the level of other well-performing Sainik Schools were praiseworthy. He also said that it was commendable that the Government of Mizoram had been able to establish such a special and good school for students in Mizoram.

He said that what makes Sainik School Chhingchhip especially different from other Sainik Schools in India is that this is the first place where girl students have been admitted, setting an example for other Sainik Schools and becoming a pioneer in this regard. He said this was a very notable achievement.

He said that Sainik Schools are excellent institutions wherever they are, and that these schools are specially meant to train students who may become officers in the Army, Navy, and Air Force. He also said that even if students of Sainik Schools do not all go on to serve in the Armed Forces, they are shaped to become exemplary citizens for society and the nation.

He reminded the students that India’s strength lies in unity and harmony amid great diversity. In this sphere of responsibility, he urged the students of Sainik School to become leaders.

source: Presbyterian Communications Board/Department hna pui ber chu thu ziak rawngbâwlnain hma a sâwn zêl theih nân, Synod leh a hnuaia pêng hrang hrangten thil chhut tûr an neih apiang fel taka chhut te, chûng zînga zawrh chi chu mipuiin an lei theih tûra a tlâwm thei anga zawrh a ni. Synod hnuaia Department hrang hrangten lehkhabu leh thil dang chhut ngai an neihte chu Synod Press-a chhut zêl tûra tih a ni a (SEC 233:39). Chutiang bawkin Synod Office leh a hnuaia Department hrang hrangten office mamawh (stationeries) an neihte chu a theih hrâm chuan Synod Bookroom-a mi lei tûra tih a ni a, Synod Bookroom-in an pêk theih loh thu an ziak thilte chauh hmun danga lei tûra tih a ni {Synod Sum Vawn Dân Bung 10:10 (1)}.
reference: The main objectives of the Presbyterian Communication Board/Department is to spread the Gospel through publication and printing words and it is responsible for the publication of any works required by Synod and all the departments under it. It also provides cheaper and accessible books for the masses as well. Synod and its departments are to publish their books and any other publication under Synod Press. (SEC 233:39). Similarly, all the departments are to buy their stationary needs from the Synod Bookroom as well. {Synod Sum VawnDân Bung 10:10 (1)}.
hypothesis: The main task of the Presbyterian Communications Board/Department is to ensure that the ministry of the written word continues to progress, by properly printing whatever materials the Synod and its various subordinate units need printed; and among these, items meant for sale are sold at as low a price as possible so that the public can buy them. The various Departments under the Synod are required to continue printing their books and other materials that need printing at the Synod Press (SEC 233:39). Likewise, the Synod Office and the various Departments under it are required, as far as possible, to purchase their office needs (stationery) from the Synod Bookroom, and only those written materials which the Synod Bookroom is unable to supply may be purchased elsewhere {Synod Financial Rules, Chapter 10:10 (1)}.

reference: ASSAM RIFLES BATTALION TO CONDUCT 8TH ROZGAR MELA FOR MIZORAM STATE 195/2023-2024 Aizawl the 26th August, 2023 - Battalion of Headquarters Inspector General Assam Rifles (East) will be conducting 8th Rozgar Mela on 28 August 2023 at 2 AR Gajraj Hall, Lakhimpur Battalion. A large number of individuals will be benefitted by the Mela. Central Government is set to organize the 8th Job Fair on 28 August 2023. This event, spanning over 25 states and more than 44 locations, will see the distribution of appointment letters to approximately 70,000 young individuals of various Departments of the Indian Government. Notably, our Honorable Prime Minister Narendra Modi will preside over the event, addressing the youth through live streaming, followed by the distribution of appointment letter to the candidates present. Assam Rifles is playing a pivotal role in organizing the Rozgar Mela for the state of Mizoram and overseeing the eventâ€™s coordination. The Honorable Minister of Minority Affairs, Mr John Barla will personally hand over appointment letter to the candidates. The Honorable Prime Minister will witness the ceremony via Video Conferencing. The Rozgar Mela is a step towards fulfillment of the duty of Government to accord highest priority to employment generation.

raw_text:
G20 Chief Coordinator Mr. Harsh Vardhan Shringla Arrives in Mizoram 3386/2022-2023 Aizawl, 27 January 2023: Today, G20 Chief Coordinator Mr. Harsh Vardhan Shringla arrived in Aizawl to review the various preparations being made by Mizoram for hosting the G20 Business-20 meeting on 2 March. At Lengpui Airport, he was received by Tourism Principal Secretary Ms. Manisha Saxena and state government officials. The Chief Coordinator was accompanied by Ministry of External Affairs Additional Secretary and Financial Advisor Mr. Vibhu Nayar and central government officials.

Mr. Harsh Vardhan Shringla first inspected the ongoing preparations at Lengpui and will also inspect the Mizoram University Auditorium and Multipurpose Hall, where the Business-20 meeting will be held. This evening, he will hold a meeting at MINECO with the G-20 Core Team and its subordinate committees, and Tourism Minister Mr. Robert Romawia Royte will also host a cultural programme and dinner for him at Chaltlang Tourist Lodge.

Tomorrow morning, Mr. Harsh Vardhan Shringla will meet Chief Minister Mr. Zoramthanga and will then depart Mizoram from Lengpui Airport.

A. Chhûnglama Chenchilhtu Thlarau Angin
Pathianin kan chhûngah a thlarau a dah a, tichuan a thlarau chu kan chhûngah chenchilhtu Thlarau a ni ang a, Pathian hriatna leh Pathian lama Krista-in kan tâna a hlenchhuah zawng zawng tawnhriatna kan nei thei dawn a ni (Rom 8:9-11). Thuthlung Hluiah chuan Pathian chuan a Thlarau chu pawnlama mihring chunga hnathawk tur ringawtin a siam a, mihring chhûngah chuan a Thlarau chu chenchilh turin a siam lo a ni. Lalpa thihna leh thawhlehna hnuah chauh chuan Pathian chuan a Thlarau chu kan hnenah min pe in, chenchilhtu Thlarau angin Thlarau chu kan chhûnga nung turin a siam a (John. 14:16-17). Hei vâng hian kan chhûnglam aṭangin Pathian leh Krista chu a puangchhuak thei a, tichuan Pathian khahna chu keini Krista ami ten kan lo dawn a kan chen theihna turin a ni (Kol. 2:9-10).
reference:
A. As the Indwelling Spirit
God puts His Spirit in us so that His Spirit may be the indwellingSpiritwithinus,thatwemayknowGodandexpe- rience all that God in Christ has accomplished for us (Rom. 8:9-11). This is the special blessing given by God in the New Testament era; it did not exist in the Old Testament. In the OldTestament,GodonlycausedHisSpirittocomefromwith- out to work upon man; He did not cause His Spirit to dwell withinman. Only after the Lord’s death and resurrection did God give His Spirit to us and cause His Spirit to dwell in us as the indwelling Spirit (John 14:16-17). Thus, He is able to reveal both God and Christ to us from within,that we in Christ may receive and enjoy the fullness of God (Col. 2:9-10).
hypothesis: A. As the Indwelling Spirit
raw_text:
A. As the Indwelling Spirit

God has put His Spirit within us, and thus His Spirit becomes the indwelling Spirit in us, so that we may have the knowledge of God and the experience of all that Christ has accomplished for us toward God (Rom. 8:9–11). This is the unique blessing that God has given in the age of the New Testament; it did not exist at all in the Old Testament. In the Old Testament, God appointed His Spirit only to work upon people outwardly; He did not appoint His Spirit to dwell within man. Only after the Lord’s death and resurrection did God give His Spirit to us and cause the Spirit to live within us as the indwelling Spirit (John 14:16–17). Because of this, He can reveal God and Christ from within us, so that we who belong to Christ may receive and partake of the fullness of God (Col. 2:9–10).

reference: In the Scriptures, only 1 John 2:27 speaks of the “teach- ing of the anointing.” We all know that anointing is a verbal noun which refers to the activity of the ointment, the mov- ing and the working of the ointment.According to the type of the Old Testament and the fulfillment of the New Testa- ment, ointment or oil in the Scripture refers to the Holy Spirit(Isa.61:1;Luke4:18).Sinceointmentoroilreferstothe Holy Spirit, the “anointing” must refer to the working of the Holy Spirit. The working of the Holy Spirit in us is like the anointing of the ointment; therefore, the Scripture calls this working of the Holy Spirit the “anointing.”
hypothesis: In the Bible, 1 John 2:27 speaks of “the anointing that teaches.” Anointing is a figurative expression referring to the act of applying oil, the action, and the work represented by the application of oil. Based on the symbolism of the Old Testament and the fulfillment of the New Testament, in Scripture oil or anointing oil signifies the Holy Spirit (Isaiah 61:1; Luke 4:18). Since oil or anointing oil refers to the Holy Spirit, “anointing” naturally refers to the work of the Holy Spirit. The work of the Holy Spirit within us is like the application of anointing oil; therefore, the Bible calls the work of the Holy Spirit “anointing.”

reference: Let me also state that people must not rush to push the government to provide for their needs. So, time management is the most important key. I think the way files are processed hierarchy-wise also needs to be revised to save more time.
hypothesis: Then, Mr. Speaker, I will not go on listing all the great initiatives and plans the government has brought forward. What I have simply been thinking in my heart today is this—that if the public becomes too impatient, we may wrongly expect the government to do everything instantly, and that is what I fear. First of all, time management will be very important. For that to happen, in government matters, what I see as the most necessary thing is this: the way our files move today—from the directorate a file comes, then in the Secretariat the Superintendent handles it first, after that the Under Secretary handles it, above the Under Secretary the Deputy Secretary handles it next, after the Deputy it goes up again to the Joint Secretary, then to the Additional Secretary, after the Additional Secretary to the Secretary, after the Secretary to the Minister. I think this part urgently needs to be improved. If the new government is to move swiftly, time will be important, and this is something that makes me think.

HPC Vice Chairman Honors Mizoram State Games Medalists

Today at the Lunglei BDO Conference Hall, a felicitation program was held under the leadership of Lunglei East AC MLA and Lunglei HPC Vice Chairman Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng for those who won medals for Lunglei East Assembly Constituency in the Mizoram State Games 2019, which concluded last December.

In the Mizoram State Games 2019, Lunglei East AC won 23 medals in various sports disciplines (7 gold, 7 silver, and 9 bronze), placing 11th in Mizoram overall and first in Lunglei District.

Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng said that it was gratifying that Lunglei East AC was able to secure such a good position in the Mizoram State Games 2019, and he expressed gratitude to the organizing committee members, the athletes, and the party leaders, saying it was the result of their hard work and dedication.

He encouraged the athletes to give their utmost so that they could achieve success beyond the state level, even at the national and international levels. He also said that elders should continue to take responsibility for guiding them properly, and that education is important no matter what path they choose to follow. He further urged them to pay attention to and clearly understand the welfare measures the government has arranged for athletes.

Those honored today were medal winners from various sports disciplines, and they were presented with certificates of honor and cash awards.

Lunglei East AC took part in 19 of the 32 sports disciplines in the Mizoram State Games and won 23 medals (7 gold, 7 silver, and 9 bronze), placing 11th in Mizoram overall and first in Lunglei District.

TRIBUTE PAID ON MAHATMA GANDHI’S BIRTH ANNIVERSARY

No. 5691/2020-2021

Along with other states of India, this morning at 7:30 a.m., to commemorate and pay tribute on the 151st birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, the Governor of Mizoram, the Chief Minister, and other important government officials laid wreaths at his statue at SBI Main Branch, Zodin Square.

Governor Pu P.S. Sreedharan Pillai, Chief Minister Pu Zoramthanga, and Deputy Chief Minister Pu Tawnluia laid wreaths and paid their respects.

The Legislative Assembly Speaker, Deputy Speaker, all Ministers and some MLAs, the AMC Mayor, as well as the Chief Secretary, Additional Chief Secretary, DGP, Aizawl DC, and SP also offered floral tributes this morning.

Gandhi’s birth anniversary is one of the few occasions declared by the Government of India as a nationwide holiday (National Holiday). In 2007, the United Nations General Assembly officially declared October 2 as the “International Day of Non-Violence.”

CHAMPHAI CLEANLINESS WEEK 2021 CONCLUDES

No.2543/2021-2022  
Aizawl, the 8th October, 2021:

Cleanliness Week 2021, observed from October 2 to 8 under the theme “Cleanliness—Starting from Our Homes and Surroundings,” concluded today at 2:00 PM at the Horticulture Complex, New Champhai.

On this occasion, the Deputy Commissioner, Pi Maria C.T. Zuali, attended as chief guest and distributed prizes to the winners of various cleanliness-related competitions. Chief guest Pi Maria C.T. Zuali said that efforts toward cleanliness should not end with the close of the week, but should be practiced throughout the year. She said that everyone shares responsibility for making Champhai District cleaner, and if each household devotes at least one hour daily to cleanliness work, the district can become the cleanest and purest of all.

She urged the people of the district to do their utmost to keep and protect Champhai District—blessed with pleasant weather, beautiful and green surroundings, lovely paddy fields, and many delightful places not found elsewhere—clean and preserved. Speaking on the importance of maintaining Champhai’s beauty and pleasantness, she said that the residents themselves are the most important, and since we ourselves are often the ones who create litter, we should not carelessly throw rubbish around when we visit the town and its beautiful surroundings.

She also mentioned that efforts are being made to install dustbins in important places and tourist spots, and added that if cleanliness awareness continues to be strongly promoted in schools, organizations, localities, offices, and churches, significant progress can be made.

Prizes for the various competitions held during Cleanliness Week were also distributed. The full list of winners in the different categories is as follows:

ELECTORAL ROLL OBSERVER VISITS KOLASIB TO REVIEW ONGOING ELECTORAL ROLL REVISION

No.6803/2020-2021  
Kolasib, 8th December 2020:

This afternoon, Pi Lalzarmawii, IAS, Secretary, AH&Veterinary Department, visited Kolasib to review the ongoing electoral roll revision work. At the DC Conference Hall, Kolasib, a meeting was held under the chairmanship of Dr. H. Lalthlangliana, District Election Officer, attended by the Electoral Registration Officer, Assistant Electoral Registration Officer, representatives of various political parties, and members of the District Level Standing Committee.

Pi Lalzarmawii, Electoral Roll Observer, said that Mizoram is recognized by the ECI as a state that consistently conducts free and fair elections, and that this is due not only to the District Election Office, officials, and various NGOs, but also to the very good cooperation of political party leaders.

The Electoral Roll Observer said that just as voting is a very important right and responsibility for all those who have attained 18 years of age under the Constitution of India, the period for revision of the electoral roll should also be given due importance, and all those who will newly attain 18 years of age by 1st January 2021 should be encouraged to ensure that their names are included during the preparation of the electoral roll.

Pu Vanlalchhuanawma Chawngthu, Election Officer, stated that the Draft Electoral Roll has already been published and that both printed copies and soft copies have been distributed to representatives of political parties. He also stated that the last date for receiving various claims and objections is 15th December 2020.

After meeting with the Standing Committee, political party representatives, and other officials, the Electoral Roll Observer also immediately visited various polling stations.

Chief Minister attends Graduation and Lamp Lighting Ceremony at RIPANS

Today, Chief Minister Pu Zoramthanga attended as chief guest the graduation celebration for students who passed this year in various Nursing and Paramedical courses at the Regional Institute of Paramedical and Nursing Sciences (RIPANS), along with the Lamp Lighting Ceremony welcoming 35 new Bachelor of Nursing students. He also presented Proficiency Awards to outstanding students.

The Chief Minister congratulated the new graduates. He said that using their skills for the welfare of fellow human beings and serving in healthcare is a very noble profession. He encouraged the newly passed students to continue their journey with diligence and sincerity and wished them increasing success.

The Chief Minister said that the government gives importance to improving healthcare and ensuring better medical care in Mizoram. For this, he said, the government alone cannot do everything, and if the state is to truly progress in the field of health, public cooperation is essential.

He also said he was pleased with the ongoing steps being taken to further develop RIPANS, and regarding the difficulties caused by staff shortages, he said efforts would be made to help as much as possible.

The Chief Minister also presented RIPANS Proficiency Awards to the best-performing graduates from each department.

At today’s function, RIPANS Director Dr. Chawngthanliana and Lamp Lighter Civil Hospital Nursing Superintendent Pi Lalrinthangi also spoke. The 35 students admitted today are first-year B.Sc. Nursing students. RIPANS Director Dr. Chawngthanliana also presented Certificates of Appreciation to the new graduates and postgraduates.

This year, a total of 180 students graduated. They are:
i) B.Sc. Nursing - 36
ii) B.Sc. MLT (Medical Laboratory Technology) - 40

Hemi hnu hian Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) leh Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Housing for All (Urban) hnuaia hamthatna dawngtute tlawhin a kawm a ni. Governor hi Environment, Forest & Climate Change Minister Pu T.J. Lalnuntluanga, Champhai South bialtu MLA ni bawk bakah DC Champhai Pu James Lalrinchhana, SP Pu Lalrinpuia Varte leh Official dangten an tawiawm a ni. Governor Pu Hari Babu Kambhampati chuan Champhai Winery tlawh theia a awm chu lawmawm a tih thu sawiin, an hmalaknate engemawchen a lo hriat tawh thu a sawi a. Champhai District-a Winery pahnih lai a awm leh loneitute intelkhawmin an kalpui chu ropui a tih thu a sawi a. Grape chingtuten harsatna an tawh chu pawi a tih thu sawiin, Sawrkarin dan thar siama hma a la chu lawmawm a ti a. Wine siam chu food processing hnuaia a awm anih thu sawiin, agriculture product-te cheibawla siam danglam value addition chu hmalakna pawimawh tak a ni, a ti a. Tun aia nasaa huang zauh leh changtlung zawka kal tura Ministry of Food Processing Industries kaltlanga hmalakna an nei chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi bawk. Governor chuan Grape chauh nilo thei dang sawr leh um theihte pawh ngaihvena huang zauh a tul thu a sawi a. An hmalak lehzelna turah duhsakna a hlan a, Mizoram mai nilo India rama loneitute tana entawntlak leh tihhmuhtu nih tum turin a chah a ni. Environment, Forest & Climate Change Minister Pu T.J. Lalnuntluanga chuan Champhai District chhunga loneitute hmalakna pawimawh tak grape sawngbawlna hmunhma Governor-in a hun hlu tak senga a tlawh chu lawmawm a ti a. Hun harsa tak paltlanga dan anga grape zawrhna tur dan thar Sawrkarin a siam thu sawiin, grape chingtuten hmabak eng tak an neih thu sawiin duhsakna a hlan a. Tun aia nasa zawka hma la a, ram ngaw humhalh nan kum tina lovah thin bansana lo nghet nei thei tura ngaihtuahna seng turin a chah a. Tun atanga reiloteah Sapthei sawngbawlna turte pawh buaipui tum anih thu sawiin, harsatna an neihte a hnena thlen hrehlo turin a chah a ni. Inkawmhona hun Packing Hall, Champhai Winery, Tlangsama hman hi Pu HS.Vanlalfakzuala, Chairman, Champhai Grape Growers Society (CGGS) chuan a kaihruai a. Pu Hrilchunglura, General Manager hnen atangin report ngaihthlak a ni a. Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Limited hotute atangin thusawi ngaihthlak a ni bawk. Mizoram hi North East India-a grape thar awm chhun leh India rama grape thar tam 5-na niin, Champhai leh Hnahlan-ah Winery a awm a. CGGS enkawl Champhai Winery hian kum 14 hmel a hmu tawh a, an Grape sawngbawl hi Bangalore Blue variety niin, vawiin thlengin Grape quintal ,15,218 an lei tling tawh a, hemi atan hian Rs 5,78,41,160/- (cheng vaibelchhe nga maktaduai sarih nuai riat singli sangkhat za leh sawmruk) an seng tawh a ni. Kum 2010 atang khan Grape quintal 918 leiin bul an tan a, kum kalta khan quintal 1144.98 an lei tling a, an Grape lakte hi herin a umna zemah an um mek a ni. Kum 2007 khan Champhai Grape Growers Association (CGGA) tih thin chu Winery din anih dawn avangin Champhai Grape Growers Society (CGGS) ti a thlak niin, Firms & Society-ah an inziahlut a ni. MIP sum cheng nuai 83 (loan) hmanga bultan niin, he loan hi November ni 9, 2020 khan Sawrkar chuan rulh let ngai lo turin grant-ah a leh sak a ni. Champhai Grape Growers Society-ah hian Governing Board Member 15 awmin kum 2 danah inthlan thin a ni a. Tun dinhmunah hian Champhai Grape Growers Society-ah hian Grape chingtu member 134 awm mekin, Staff leh Worker mi 30, Executive Member 9 leh Office Bearer 6 an awm mek bawk a. Champhai Grape Growers Society hnuaiah hian Branch 9 awm mekin mumal taka inenkawlna kalpui thin a ni. CGGS hian Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MOFPI) kaltlangin project an kalpui mek a. DC Office kaltlangin Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) hnuaiah Commerce & Industries Department hnuaiah project dil mek a ni bawk a. Dan thar hnuaiah Winery License an nei fel tawh a, State pawn thlenga hralhchhuak thei turin hmachhawp an nei a ni. Champhai Winery a tlawh zawh hian Governor chuan BPL family-te tana a thlawna eirawngbawlna gas connection pekna scheme, Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) kaltlanga hamthatna dawngtu leh khawpuia cheng insak tanpuina scheme, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Housing for All (Urban) dawngtu Tlangsam ami te a tlawh a; scheme awmzia leh tangkainate a sawifiah a, an hmuh dan leh chhawr tangkai dante a zawt nghal bawk. reference: Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati visits Champhai Tlangsam Winery 326/2022-2023 Aizawl, the 1st February 2023 : Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati, who is on a two-day tour of Champhai District visited the Tlangsam Winery on the outskirt of Champhai Town this evening. At the site, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati was given an escorted tour to various units by the managing officers of the winery. Thereafter, a short program was held at B Remmawia Packing hall, Champhai Winery. Governor Hari Babu expressed his delight in visiting the factory started, owned, and managed by a society of farmers. He was particularly appreciative of having witness the production centre where the determined farmers themselves added value to their products. He congratulated the Champhai Grape Growers Society and the Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Ltd. Governor welcomed the ambitious proposal to upgrade these wineries at Champhai and Hnahlan to accomodate the growing production of the Grapes in these areas. He extended his support for this proposal and if necessary, he agreed to discuss the matter with the authorities in the Ministry of Food Processing Industries(MoFPI). On behalf of Champhai Winery, Pu Hrilchunglura, General Manager, Champhai Grape Growers Society(GGGS) gave a report. The Winery was started in 2007. After 14 years of existence with the production actually started in 2010 the Winery has now grown. At present the society has 134 members. The fruit is of Bangalore Blue variety. During last year the Winery bought 1144.98 qts of grapes. As the grape production increases, CGGS submitted two projects - one project to MoFPI and another project to state department under Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK). GOVERNOR HARI BABU KAMBHAMPATI VISITS CHAMPHAI WINERY, MEETS BENEFICIARIES OF PMUY AND PMAY-HFA URBAN

3449/2022-2023  
Champhai, 1st February, 2023:

Mizoram Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati, who is on a two-day visit to Champhai, this afternoon visited Champhai Winery at Tlangsam and reviewed its activities; he also met the leaders of the Champhai Grape Growers Society and the Hnahlan Grape Growers and Processing Co-operative Society Limited. After this, he visited and met beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Housing for All (Urban).

The Governor was accompanied by Environment, Forest & Climate Change Minister T.J. Lalnuntluanga, who is also the MLA of Champhai South, along with DC Champhai James Lalrinchhana, SP Lalrinpuia Varte, and other officials.

Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati said he was pleased to be able to visit Champhai Winery and that he had already heard something about its activities. He said it was commendable that there are two wineries in Champhai district and that they are being run in coordination with the farmers. He expressed concern over the difficulties faced by grape growers and welcomed the Government’s initiative in framing new rules. He said wine-making comes under food processing, and value addition through processing agricultural products is a very important initiative. He also said he appreciated the steps being taken through the Ministry of Food Processing Industries to expand further and move ahead more effectively than at present.

The Governor said attention should be given not only to grapes but also to expanding into other fruits and products that can be processed. He conveyed his good wishes for their continued efforts and urged them to aim to become a model and an inspiration not only for Mizoram but for farmers across India.

Environment, Forest & Climate Change Minister T.J. Lalnuntluanga said he was happy that the Governor had spent his valuable time visiting this important grape-processing centre, which is a significant initiative of the farmers within Champhai district. He said that after passing through a very difficult period, the Government had framed new rules for the lawful sale of grapes, and he conveyed his good wishes while speaking of the important role of grape growers. hypothesis: 5th STATE LEVEL TASK FORCE MEETING. Today at 11 AM, the members of the State Level Task Force (SLTF) on the National Railway Project held a meeting at the I&PR Conference Hall under the chairmanship of Task Force Chairman Pu Zasanga, IPS (Rtd). In this meeting, Land Acquisition, Forest Clearance, the proposal for Khanpui Railway Station, and the construction of a Railway Station at Sihhmui were discussed. Pu V.P. Srivastava, Chief Engineer, NF Railways, Guwahati, presented a report on the work completed so far; he said that the Final Location Survey (FLS) was continuing smoothly, and that the GPS, traversing, and topography survey for the stretch between Bairabi and Sairang (51.21 kms) had all been completed. He also stated that the final stacking alignment, which had already begun on 17th April 2010 from Bairabi and Hortoki, was targeted for completion by 31st May 2010. In order to inspect the work already carried out by NF Railways and to enable clearer progress on matters relating to Land Acquisition and Forest Clearance, it was decided that the three departments—Revenue, Forest, and Railways—would conduct a joint survey on 26th April 2010 under the leadership of the Kolasib Deputy Commissioner.

Srivastava, Chief Engineer, NF Railways, Guwahati, presented a report on the work completed so far; he said that the Final Location Survey (FLS) was continuing smoothly, and that the GPS, traversing, and topography survey for the stretch between Bairabi and Sairang (51.21 kms) had all been completed. He also stated that the final stacking alignment, which had already begun on 17th April 2010 from Bairabi and Hortoki, was targeted for completion by 31st May 2010. raw_text:
PU LAWMAWMA TOCHHAWNG, VICE CHAIRMAN, HPC, INAUGURATES THE RENOVATED LUNGLEI POLICE STATION BUILDING

1328/2023-2025  
Lunglei; 1st August, 2023:

Today at 11:30 a.m., the renovated Ground Floor of the Lunglei Police Station Building was inaugurated by chief guest Pu Lawmawma Tochhawng, Vice Chairman, HPC, Lunglei. The funds for the renovation of the building were received from the Lunglei High Powered Committee Fund.

An amount of Rs. 15 lakh each was sanctioned from the HPC Fund for the renovation of the Ground Floor and the 1st Floor. The Ground Floor, which was inaugurated today, was renovated using the 2022–2023 fund. For the renovation of the 1st Floor, Rs. 15 lakh has already been sanctioned for 2023–2024, and the Police Department can carry out the renovation work and begin it at any time.

The Lunglei Police Station building was originally constructed in 1991. It is located in the heart of Lunglei town, and the building had become very old.

Speaking at today’s inauguration of the renovated Police Station Building, Pu Lawmawma said that Lunglei Police Station currently holds the title of Best Police Station in India. After being assessed through various parameters, the police station that earned the distinction of being the best in the whole country is now being renovated to become the best police station building in Mizoram as well, which is very fitting for its status as the best. He said that while he congratulates the police, he too feels proud to be associated with it.

Pu Lawmawma also said that the way the Lunglei Police Station staff carried out the renovation work with a sense of ownership was admirable, and that it is a pleasure to work together with people who deserve praise.

The chief guest further urged the Lunglei Police to strive to become the best in all India particularly in the area of traffic management within their sphere of work. He also expressed the hope that the police station would be a place where the public can come without hesitation and freely bring their problems and grievances, and that with this new building, the PS staff too would continue to warmly and cheerfully receive those who come to them.

Today’s inauguration programme for the renovated building was held at the police station gate. The programme was chaired by Pu K. Beihmotaosa

Aizawl, the 8th March, 2024:

NABARD, Mizoram Regional Office, Aizawl, today celebrated International Women’s Day (IWD) 2024 at HYVE City Hall, Aizawl. As part of IWD, a two-day exhibition was organised, in which Self Help Groups, Farmer Producer Organizations, and Women Entrepreneurs displayed their new products and creations.

The function organised for today’s IWD celebration and inauguration of the exhibition was graced by Pi H. Lalchhandami, CEO, MzSRLM, as the chief guest. Speaking about the Rural Livelihood Mission initiatives aimed at helping women earn more income and advance in their livelihoods, she also expressed gratitude for the strong cooperation they have with NABARD in their efforts.

Pu KVSSLV Prasada Rao, General Manager/OIC, NABARD, said at the programme that NABARD has various schemes through which Self Help Groups can benefit for the empowerment of women, including Skill Development, Tribal Development, and Micro Enterprise Development.

The theme for today’s IWD celebration was “Count Her In: Accelerating Gender Equality through Economic Empowerment.” On the occasion, Pi Lalrohlupuii, SMS, Home Science, KVK, Aizawl, and Pi Lalhlupuii Ralte, Proprietor, Zo Bio Hub, also spoke.

Pu T. Khup Guite, Deputy General Manager, NABARD, SHG members, and successful women entrepreneurs were present.

Aizawl, the 14th July, 2021:

Dr. Lalhriatzuali Ralte, Aizawl District Commissioner, received various important items for fighting the Covid-19 pandemic from World Vision India, Chennai, on July 12, 2021.

The Covid-19 fighting materials sent by World Vision to the Aizawl DC Office are: Medical grade N-95 masks - 1500 pcs, Surgical masks - 2000 pcs, Face shields - 1000 pcs, Surgical gloves - 1000 pcs, Pulse oximeters - 150 pcs, and PPE kits - 500 pcs.

These items will be distributed from the DC Office for useful use by those who need them.

SIAHA DC MAKES A SURPRISE VISIT TO SOME OFFICES

The Deputy Commissioner of Siaha District, Pu Bhupesh Chaudhary, IAS, made a surprise visit to some offices this morning.

Pu Bhupesh said that his “surprised visit” was not intended to find fault with or embarrass the offices for improper functioning, but to understand how the various offices are being run and to listen to the difficulties they face. At the same time, the DC said he is closely observing the functioning and work culture of the various offices under his charge, and he wants it to be known that he will be very displeased with staff who neglect their duties or are unwilling to remain at their posts.

The offices visited today were: ITI (Industrial Training Institute), Excise & Narcotics Office, Mizofed, Printing & Stationery Depot, and the FCS & Consumer Affairs Godown.

Such surprise visits will continue to be made whenever time permits, and there is an intention to visit all offices and educational institutions under the Government of Mizoram.

Accompanying the DC during today’s surprise visit were Pu Amol Srivastava, IAS, Assistant Commissioner, Pu H. Zonunmawia, Election Officer, and Pu N. Vabeiratlua, DIPRO.

raw_text:
DISTRICT TASK FORCE COMMITTEE HOLDS EMERGENCY MEETING ON COVID-19 IN SIAHA

Today at 2:00 PM, the District Task Force Committee held an emergency meeting on COVID-19 at the DC Conference Hall. The committee held an urgent discussion on how Siaha district could be protected from COVID-19.

On 7/3/2020, the District Magistrate had already ordered the closure of routes connecting Myanmar through 10 villages in Siaha district: Lopu, Chapi, Khaikhy, Zyhno, Lodaw, Lomasu, Iana, Siasi, Laki, and Khopai. In addition, orders had also been issued to set up check posts at three inter-district border crossing points: Kaochao, Tipi Ferry, and Tlapi.

In all these 13 villages/points, Gram Sabhas are to be convened and sensitization campaigns are to be carried out, and the Siaha BDO and Tipa BDO have already gone out today for this purpose.

Today’s meeting also resolved to request that a joint committee be formed in each of these 13 villages, consisting of the Church, NGOs, and Village Councils, and that these joint committees should monitor the routes/paths connecting their villages with Myanmar. It was also resolved to invite support from the MADC Forest Department and Indian soldiers stationed in the border area villages.

On 13 and 14 March 2020, joint teams comprising medical personnel, NGO leaders, Joint VC leaders, police, and the DC office will visit these 13 villages, inspect how they are monitoring routes connecting with Myanmar as a preventive measure against COVID-19, and immediately conduct sensitization campaigns.

At present, the Siaha Medical Office has only one Thermal Infrared Sensor machine for detecting fever and only 15 sets of Personal Protection Equipment (PPE). It has been reported that two more TIRS machines are on the way. These TIRS machines will be placed at the three check posts.

Apart from the TIRS, the medical department will also place Self Reporting Forms at all three check points. Based on the TIRS screening and the Self Reporting Forms, travelers entering Siaha district who are suspected of carrying COVID-19 will be kept in isolation for 20 days.

We enjoy the manna and we enjoy the rock with the living water. Do you have such an experience day by day? Many of you can boldly say that you do.
