CHAMPHAI DISTRICT CONSULTATIVE COMMITTEE (DCC) / DISTRICT LEVEL REVIEW COMMITTEE (DLRC) MEETING No.7432/2020-2021

The Champhai District Consultative Committee (DCC) / District Level Review Committee (DLRC), chaired by Pi Maria C.T. Zuali, Deputy Commissioner of Champhai, met today at the DC Conference Hall. They reviewed the activities of banks and various stakeholders within the two RD Blocks of Champhai District up to the end of the September 2020 quarter, and the Potential Credit Linked Plan (PLP) 2021–2022 for Champhai District prepared by NABARD was released by Deputy Commissioner Pi Maria C.T. Zuali.

Pi Maria C.T. Zuali said that banking facilities need to be expanded to all sections of the people, and that wider awareness programmes are very necessary so that those who are entitled to benefits through banks can actually receive them. She urged bank officials to translate and issue important documents and application forms in Mizo so that the public can better understand how to make proper use of banks and become more clearly aware of the benefits available through them. She also urged support for the poor and the needy so that they may receive the available benefits and be helped toward self-reliance.

She expressed concern over the very low Credit Deposit Ratio comparing deposits and advances in banks, and urged greater openness and effort to achieve a better Credit Deposit Ratio. She also urged borrowers to take loan repayment seriously, and said that the DC Office would fully support bankers in pursuing defaulters.

At the meeting, after Pu L. Lawmvela, Lead District Manager (LDM), SBI Lead Bank Office Champhai, delivered the welcome address, a review was conducted of the work and progress of various banks in Champhai District up to the end of the September 2020 quarter, and future plans were also discussed.

As presented in the meeting, the average Credit Deposit (CD) Ratio of various banks in Champhai District up to the end of the September 2020 quarter was 44.71%, which was an increase of 2.28% over the June quarter-end CD Ratio of 42.43%; however, it still did not reach the benchmark CD Ratio of 60%.

Speaking of how he works closely with Mizo community and many sub-tribes of Mizoram in his constituency, he expressed his optimism for an enduring friendship and partnership in all sectors. THE CORPORATE PRIESTHOOD WITH THE URIM AND THUMMIM

The second aspect of the anointing is the corporate priesthood with the Urim and Thummim. What is the corporate priesthood? This is something wonderful and glorious. The corporate priesthood includes fellowship with the Lord, life, and the ministry of His presence. The corporate priesthood is the gathered people who continually have fellowship with the Lord. When we have fellowship with the Lord, remain one with Him day by day and at all times, and live, serve, and act in this living fellowship, then we are the corporate priesthood.

Governor chuan Dr SK Prasad leh a thawhna hmuna thuneituten Mizoramah zirlai te tan Space Technology zir theihna hun remchang an rawn zawn sak chu lawmawm a tih thu a sawi a. Dr SK Prasad chuan Prime Minister hmathlir angin India thalaite chu space technology lamah thiamna sang zawk nei tur leh India ram chu a hmahruaitu a nih theih nan chher hriam mek an ni a ti a. Dr Prasad chuan a lo kal chhan tak chu Higher Secondary atanga University Degree zirlaite tan Space Technology zirna an kalpui mek chu Mizorama zirlaite rawn hmelhriat tir a ni a ti a. Hemi kawngah hian Governor leh state sawrkar hotute thlawpna a rawn ngen bakah a bikin science lam zirna kaihhnawiha hotute thawhpuiah a rawn sawm tih a sawi bawk a ni. In this regard, he advised Dr SK Prasad and the institutions he represented to have close coordination with the authorities of Higher & Technical Education Department, Mizoram University, NIT Mizoram, Polytechnics, Science & Technology Department and Science Teachers Association Of Mizoram. Dr SK Prasad apprised the Governor of their initiatives in teaching the teams of students and assigning them important science projects like making mini satellites and other space technology. He told Governor that his purpose of visiting is identifying the institutions with whom they will have a series of correspondences to initiate enrollment of the students in the program. raw_text:
Governor Hari Babu and the ITCA chief discuss opportunities for talented students in Mizoram to study space technology

1070/2022-2023  
Aizawl, 28th June 2022:

This morning, Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati met Dr. S.K. Prasad, founder member and advisory council member of the Indian Technology Congress Association (ITCA), Bangalore, at Raj Bhavan.

During the meeting, they discussed how to identify talented students in Mizoram who are interested in studying space technology and how they could be given opportunities to pursue such studies.

Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati said that students in Mizoram are highly capable academically and are intellectually on par with students elsewhere. He said that if avenues for studying space technology are opened up, they would be able to excel in the field.

The Governor expressed appreciation that Dr. S.K. Prasad and the authorities of his organization were exploring ways to create opportunities for students in Mizoram to study space technology.

In this regard, the ITCA leaders were advised to approach the Higher & Technical Education Department, Mizoram University, NIT Mizoram, the Polytechnics, the Science & Technology Department, and the Science Teachers Association of Mizoram. It was said that through consultation with them, it would be easier to identify more capable students who are interested in studying space technology.

Dr. S.K. Prasad said that, in line with the Prime Minister’s vision, efforts are being made to equip India’s youth with higher expertise in space technology so that India can become a leader in the field.

As part of this initiative, under the Students’ Satellites 75 project, 75 student teams will be selected this year to build mini satellites, with the aim of completing 75 projects. He said that students from across India would compete in this project and 75 teams would be selected.

He added that this project could also open up opportunities for students from Mizoram to participate.

Dr. Prasad said that the main purpose of his visit was to introduce to students in Mizoram the space technology education programme being carried out for students from Higher Secondary level up to University Degree level.

In this connection, he sought the support of the Governor and state government officials, and also invited the cooperation of those particularly associated with science education.

source: CHAMPHAI DISTRICT TASK FORCE ON CORONA VIRUS OUTBREAK THUKHAWM Tunlaia China leh khawvel ram dangte ngaihven hlawh tak Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) natna leng mek laka Champhai District lo him leh invenlawkna tura din, District Task Force on Corona Virus Outbreak chu a vawikhatna turin vawiin chawhnu khan Bawrhsap Pu SL Naveen, IAS hovin DC Conference Hall-ah an thukhawm. Meeting-ah hian Champhai District chu International Border-a awm anih avangin Novel Coronavirus leng darh zel tur laka fimkhur angaih thu tarlan niin, meeting chuan ramri kaltlanga veivak leh sumdawng thinte chu he natna len mekna hmun leh a chhehvelte laka fimkhur turin a ngen a. He hunah hian mihring veivak leh ran khuahkhirh anih dante ngaihthlak a ni bawk a. Champhai District ep Myanmar ram District-te nena inbiakpawh leh inzaitawn zela hmalak a tul thu pawh tarlan a ni a. District Task Force on Coronavirus Outbreak chuan ramri depa awm khuate chu tlawhchhuaka mipuite hnena zirtirna zau zawk kalpui nise, ramri kaltlanga lutte hriselna endik pahin chhui zui ngai awmte pawh chhuichian ni se a ti a. Champhai District Hospital-a Isolation Ward ruahman ni se tih bakah mamawh tur ang budget-te pawh a rang lama siama thuneitu sang zawk hnena thlen nise tih a ni. District Level Task Force on Corona Virus Outbreak hi Mizoram State Health Minister leh H&FW Department hotute January Ni 30, 2020 a thukhawm in an din tak State Level Task Force on Mitigation of Corona Virus duh dan anga district tina hma lo la tur a din a ni. Champhai District-a Zokhawtharah February Ni 4, 2020 atang khan Medical Screening hi kalpui tan a ni a, khualzinte chinchang zawhfiah leh a tul anga endik hna hi kalpui thin niin, Self Reporting Form mumal tak kalpui tan a ni tawh bawk. reference: CHAMPHAI DISTRICT TASK FORCE ON CORONA VIRUS OUTBREAK HELD MEETING In pursuance of the decision made by Mizoram State Level Task Force on Mitigation of Corona Virus, Champhai District Task Force on Corona Virus was formed recently and held its first meeting at DC Conference Hall, yesterday. The meeting was presided over by Pu SL Naveen, IAS Deputy Commissioner Champhai. Given its strategic location, Champhai district being located nearby International Border, the meeting mentioned the needs for proper medical screening at Zokhawthar and restriction on movement particularly travellers based on their travelling history. To boost up the preventive measures, the meeting highlighted the importance of fostering better coordination with the neighbouring district administration of Myanmar. raw_text:
CHAMPHAI DISTRICT TASK FORCE ON CORONAVIRUS OUTBREAK MEETING

To ensure the safety and preparedness of Champhai District against the ongoing spread of the Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV), which is currently drawing serious concern in China and other countries around the world, the District Task Force on Coronavirus Outbreak held its first meeting this afternoon at the DC Conference Hall under the chairmanship of Deputy Commissioner Pu S.L. Naveen, IAS.

At the meeting, it was pointed out that since Champhai District is located on an international border, there is a need for vigilance against the possible spread of the Novel Coronavirus. The meeting appealed to travelers and traders crossing the border to remain cautious regarding areas affected by the outbreak and surrounding regions. Matters relating to human travel and the movement of animals were also discussed.

It was also stated that Champhai District needs to maintain communication and coordination with neighboring districts in Myanmar and continue taking necessary steps. The District Task Force on Coronavirus Outbreak decided that awareness and educational activities should be carried out more extensively among people in villages along the border, and that health screening of those entering through the border should be conducted, with proper tracing of persons requiring follow-up.

It was further decided that an Isolation Ward should be arranged at Champhai District Hospital, and that the required budget should be prepared quickly and submitted to higher authorities.

The District Level Task Force on Coronavirus Outbreak was constituted in line with the decision of the State Level Task Force on Mitigation of Coronavirus, which was formed at a meeting held on January 30, 2020, by the Mizoram State Health Minister and officials of the Health & Family Welfare Department, so that each district could begin taking action.

Medical screening at Zokhawthar in Champhai District began on February 4, 2020. Verification of travelers’ details and necessary examinations are being carried out regularly, and a proper Self Reporting Form has also already been introduced.

The Champhai District Task Force on Coronavirus Outbreak has also provided Mobile Nos. 8588009756 / 9436376607 as contact numbers for those in need.

source:
Kan ngaihthlak ang khan, September Ni 24, 2020-ah Govt. of India notification 
a awm a, chu mi dungzuiin State tinah buatsaih a ni bawk a. Amaherawhchu, tui hi State 
List a nih angin state tin sorkar chu a thu viau mai a. Tunah hian State 16 leh UT 5-ah 
he Dan hi neih a ni tawh a. Tin, State 11-ah ngaihtuah mek a ni bawk a. State 4 hi chuan 
an ramah he Dan neih hi tul an ti lova, chungte chu - Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, 
Sikkim leh Tripura te an ni. Mizoram-ah erawh chuan a tul ngawih ngawihin ka hria a. 
Amaherawhchu, control a ngai a ni. Tute’n emaw an duh duhna hmunah an pump 
chhuak rikngawt kha chu a him lova, lei hnuaia water table te pawh tibuai thei a ni. 
Chuvangin, hetianga Dan lo awm hi a tha ka ti a. Chapter 6, section 29(C)-ah khan 
hremna Dan a awm a.
reference:
As we have listened, there was a Government of India notification on September 
24, 2020, and based on that, all the states followed. But ‘water’ falls under the state list, 
so the state government has the authority. 16 states and 5 UTs currently have a similar
act regarding this, and 11 states are currently discussing this Act. Four states regarded 
it as unnecessary to have this Act, these are Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Sikkim, and 
Tripura. On the other hand, I believe Mizoram urgently requires this Act, but there must 
be a way to control it. Whoever is capable of doing it must not attempt to pump out 
water, as it could disturb the water tables. So, it is good that such acts as these exist. 
Chapter 6, Section 29 (C), talks about penalties for violators.
hypothesis: As we heard, on 24 September 2020 there was a notification from the Government of India, and following that, arrangements were also made in each state. However, since water falls under the State List, each state government has full authority over it. At present, this law has already been adopted in 16 states and 5 Union Territories. It is also under consideration in 11 states. Four states do not consider it necessary to have this law in their territories; they are Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Sikkim, and Tripura. In Mizoram, however, I think it is very necessary. Even so, it needs control. If people simply drill borewells wherever they want, it is not safe and may also disturb the underground water table. Therefore, I think it is good to have such a law. In Chapter 6, Section 29(C), there is a penal provision.
raw_text: As we heard, on 24 September 2020 there was a notification from the Government of India, and following that, arrangements were also made in each state. However, since water falls under the State List, each state government has full authority over it. At present, this law has already been adopted in 16 states and 5 Union Territories. It is also under consideration in 11 states. Four states do not consider it necessary to have this law in their territories; they are Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Sikkim, and Tripura. In Mizoram, however, I think it is very necessary. Even so, it needs control. If people simply drill borewells wherever they want, it is not safe and may also disturb the underground water table. Therefore, I think it is good to have such a law. In Chapter 6, Section 29(C), there is a penal provision.

raw_text:
RASHTRIYA EKTA DIWAS CELEBRATED GRANDLY

This morning, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) was celebrated at AR Ground, with Deputy Chief Minister Pu Tawnluia as the chief guest. Addressing the gathering, chief guest Pu Tawnluia said that the Government of India had declared October 31 as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) in commemoration of the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who worked tirelessly for the unity of India.

The Deputy Chief Minister said that Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) has been observed since 2014, and that today marks its sixth observance. He said that in 1917, after listening to Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel dedicated himself fully to the cause of India, worked courageously, and came to be known as the “Iron Man of India.” He also said that when the British were about to leave India, Patel played a major role in bringing together more than 500 princely states under India.

Chief guest Pu Tawnluia called upon those gathered to work for the nation and to continue preserving unity, following the example of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, one of the important figures in India’s freedom struggle.

Chief Secretary Pu Lalnunmawia Chuaungo administered the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas pledge to all those present on the occasion.

Nine contingents—Assam Rifles, BSF, 1st Battalion MAP, 3rd Battalion MAP, 5th IR Battalion, Home Guard, 225 Battalion CRPF, One Mizo Air Squadron NCC, and 20 Mizo Independent Company NCC—took part in the parade. The Parade Commander was Inspector PC Vanlalsawma of MAP, and the Assam Rifles Band Party also played the National Anthem.

As part of the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebration, at 7 a.m. 500 schoolchildren held a Run for Unity from Sikulpuikawn and Chanmari and assembled at AR Ground.

MIZORAM POLICE PRESS STATEMENT 566/2023-2024

The Mizoram Police Media Cell has issued the following message to the public regarding the Digital Payment System:

ADVISORY ON DIGITAL PAYMENT FRAUD:

As the use of Digital Payment Systems is increasing rapidly, fraud related to it is also rising sharply even in Mizoram. In this internet age, fraudsters are constantly finding new ways to cheat, targeting people who are unsuspecting and easy to deceive.

At present, more than 75% of the cyber crime cases registered in Mizoram are related to online financial fraud. Therefore, for our safety against such fraud, Mizoram Police requests the public to follow the points given below:

Do not share your banking password, OTP, Debit Card/Credit Card details with anyone.

If you are the one receiving money, do not scan any QR Code. No scanning is required for receiving money; scanning is only needed for sending money.

Be aware that phishing scammers are always trying to steal your important Bank and UPI information. Do not casually enter unknown emails, websites, or suspicious links.

When buying things online, searching for products through a Search Engine is often not safe enough. Therefore, always browse and buy only from known online shopping websites.

Be aware that offers claiming you can earn money without doing anything, or investment schemes promising unusually high and safe returns, or anything that appears too good to be true, are generally scams.

Be cautious of applications and websites claiming they can provide loans easily and quickly. To give loans, they ask for all kinds of personal information, and these are often later used for blackmail. Even if you use a Loan App, make sure it is approved by RBI.

Also be aware that people posing as Police/Army personnel and selling goods online at very low prices are generally criminals.

We once again urge the public to be as cautious as possible in all matters involving online financial transactions. If you become a victim of such fraud, you may file a complaint through the Cyber Helpline 1930 or at www.cybercrime.gov.in.

THE FOLLOWING IS THE PROCEDURE FOR FILING A COMPLAINT AT www.cybercrime.gov.in

1. Open www.cybercrime.gov.in from any mobile or computer browser (Google, Safari, etc.).

The work of revising the Electoral Roll for all 40 Assembly Constituencies of Mizoram with reference to January 1, 2010 has been completed.
